cases.description: When both parameters are null the method should throw NPE because the root JSON node is required.
When the JSON node is null but a customizer is supplied the method must still reject the call with NPE.
A null customizer is allowed; the method should behave as if no customizer was provided and return an empty validation result for a valid empty object.
When the customizer sets a flag that the validator checks (e.g., "skip"), the validator should bypass further validation and return an empty set.
If the customizer itself throws an exception, the validate method must propagate that exception.
A JSON document that satisfies the schema (e.g., required fields, correct types) should produce an empty validation message set.
An empty array that conforms to an "array" type schema should also return an empty set.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'type' and path '/age'
cases.description: When a property has an invalid type (string instead of integer) the validator must return a ValidationMessage describing the type error.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'required' and path ''
cases.description: When required properties are missing the validator must return a required‑field ValidationMessage.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'additionalProperties' and path ''
cases.description: When additionalProperties is false and an unexpected property is present, a corresponding ValidationMessage must be produced.
If the schema contains a recursive anchor (isRecursiveAnchor() == true) and the instance resolves correctly, validation should succeed without infinite recursion.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'maxDepth' (or similar) if implementation limits recursion
cases.description: When the recursive anchor leads to a depth that exceeds the validator’s recursion limit, an appropriate ValidationMessage must be returned.
When the schema is marked as a resource root (isSchemaResourceRoot() == true) the validator should treat $id resolution accordingly and still validate successfully.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'type' and path ''
cases.description: The schema expects an object at the root, but an array is supplied; validation should report a type error at the root path.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'type' and path ''
cases.description: When the root JSON node is a primitive string while the schema requires an object, a type ValidationMessage must be returned.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'format' and path '/email'
cases.description: The schema defines a regex/pattern for the "email" property; providing a non‑matching value should yield a format ValidationMessage.
A correctly formatted email satisfies the pattern constraint, resulting in no validation messages.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'enum' and path '/status'
cases.description: The "status" property is limited to a set of allowed enum values; an out‑of‑range value must generate an enum ValidationMessage.
A value that belongs to the defined enum list passes validation without errors.
The schema uses oneOf to allow either a numeric or a string representation; providing a number satisfies one branch, so validation succeeds.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'oneOf' and path '/value'
cases.description: A boolean does not match any of the oneOf alternatives (number or string), therefore a oneOf ValidationMessage should be produced.
The schema requires an array of strings; an array where every element is a string validates without errors.

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'type' and path '/1'
cases.description: The second element is an integer while the schema expects strings; a type ValidationMessage should be reported at the offending index.

group: Null customizer with non‑empty valid object

cases.description: A null executionCustomizer should be treated as a no‑op; a valid object must still produce an empty validation result.
If the customizer throws a RuntimeException (not IllegalStateException), the validate method must propagate it unchanged.

group: Deep nesting exceeding max depth without recursive anchor

cases.expected: Set containing ValidationMessage with type 'maxDepth' (or similar)
cases.description: When the instance depth exceeds the validator's configured maximum depth and the schema does not use a recursive anchor, validation should stop and report a maxDepth ValidationMessage.

The schema contains a $ref with an invalid percent‑encoding (e.g., "%ZZ"). When validate() attempts to resolve the reference it calls URLDecoder.decode, which throws UnsupportedEncodingException. The method must propagate this exception.

The schema node defines an unknown type value (e.g., "type": "unknownType"). During validator initialization JsonSchema should detect the illegal type and throw IllegalArgumentException before any validation occurs.

The schema includes a custom keyword that the library does not recognise (e.g., "fooValidator": true). While building the validator list JsonSchema throws UnsupportedOperationException, which must be propagated by validate().

The schema contains a circular $ref chain that does not involve a recursive anchor. When validate() follows the references it recurses indefinitely, eventually causing a StackOverflowError. The method should let this error surface.

group: ExecutionCustomizer throws checked exception wrapped in RuntimeException

input.value: consumer -> { try { throw new java.io.IOException("io fail"); } catch (Exception e) { throw new RuntimeException(e); } }

cases.description: The customizer throws a checked exception (IOException) which is wrapped in a RuntimeException. validate() must propagate the RuntimeException unchanged.
